correctness.rationale: T=J-I diagonalization gives exact two-site probabilities and r_d; spatial DFT gives every Gram eigenvalue and multiplicity, with an exact rank-one precision correction. Positivity is checked for all a>=2,n>=3. The extremal inequality is proved uniformly: even n by two-sided spectral bounds, odd n with a>=3 via n=3,5 and n>=7 inequalities, and ternary odd n separately. The singular triangle and unique ternary pentagon maximize are explicitly evaluated. The accompanying standalone checker passed 12 exact finite enumerations, 54 rational two-point moments, 900 exact colour-pair cells, 54 DFT checks and over 3000 finite inequality spot checks. The finite checks are not substituted for the all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: Proper graph colourings provide a natural nonlinear support for Fourier coordinate reconstruction. The result is a complete infinite-family Gram classification with a sharp and nontrivially attained global conditioning constant, exactly identifying singularity and the exceptional worst case. The sparse precision-matrix formula enables local algebraic inversion up to one global correction. Unlike a routine fixed-parameter computation, the proof solves an extremal problem jointly over all lengths and colour counts, whose maximizing ternary pentagon differs from both the smallest admissible and asymptotic regimes.
